entries.windows: SetPriorityClass does not validate the value as a whole: it takes the recognised class bits out of it and the lowest class wins, IDLE first. A value carrying at least one recognised bit succeeds; a nonzero value carrying none is refused like 0, with FALSE and ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87). REALTIME (0x100) returns TRUE but leaves the class at HIGH (0x80) without SeIncreaseBasePriorityPrivilege. The precedence among the recognised bits is a strict order, and it is the inverse of scheduling priority: the lowest class always wins. Over all fifteen pairs, IDLE beats all five others, BELOW_NORMAL four, NORMAL three, ABOVE_NORMAL two, HIGH one, and REALTIME none.
entries.evidence: probed here, resetting to NORMAL between calls. Recognised alone: 0x20->0x20, 0x40->0x40, 0x80->0x80, 0x4000->0x4000, 0x8000->0x8000, 0x100->1 err=0 but class 0x80. IDLE wins over the rest: 0x60, 0xc0, 0x140, 0x4040 all -> 0x40. 0x12345 (has 0x40 and 0x100) -> 0x40, and 0x12305, the same value with 0x40 cleared, -> 0x80 through its 0x100. No recognised bit: 0x1, 0x2, 0x8, 0x10, 0x200, 0x1000, 0x10000 all -> 0 err=87. Round 2, every pair probed: 0x4020 and 0x4080 -> BELOW_NORMAL, 0x8020 -> NORMAL, 0x8080 -> ABOVE_NORMAL, 0xa0 and 0x120 -> NORMAL, 0x180 -> HIGH, 0x4100 -> BELOW_NORMAL, 0x8100 -> ABOVE_NORMAL, 0xc000 -> BELOW_NORMAL, and every pair containing IDLE -> IDLE.
entries.note: A real divergence, and the rule is not the one it first looks like: it is not that the IDLE bit means IDLE, but that unrecognised bits are ignored while any recognised one decides, with IDLE taking precedence. So an unknown value is refused when it carries no class bit at all, which means gala cannot simply accept every nonzero value either. The REALTIME downgrade is a second, separate thing to match. Round 2, from ROADMAP WD Next item 1. So the Linux side's "gala takes the lowest class for now" is already right, and the test can assert it. Answers the open probe for two class bits with neither being IDLE's. MAPPING IS A GUESS for check 36 (got 0x10000000): the Linux side showed one of these cannot be the line counted to (kernel32_thread_test 36 maps to a value masked to 16 bits, which cannot give 0x10000000).
